text:
The Isolde, lead vessel of the Calder Strait Ferry Authority's new Isolde-class fleet, carried its first paying passengers between Varnholm and Ostrel on 14 March 2031. It carries up to 650 passengers.

I stood on the Varnholm quay that morning and heard Captain Marguerite Tolliver, the Authority's Fleet Operations Director, confirm the figure at the launch briefing. She said the ship is licensed for 650 passengers plus 90 vehicles.

The Authority's Certificate of Passenger Capacity, Ref. CSFA-IS-0412, which was issued after the vessel's final safety inspection, sets out the same limit. Reporters were shown the document at the briefing.

The Isolde measures 128 meters in length, which makes it a notable presence beside the old harbour wall. Boarding began shortly after the briefing and, from the quay, appeared orderly.
